messages.content: Find a picnic spot in Miami.

function.name: local_fauna

message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to some great picnic-friendly spots around Miami: | Spot | Location & Highlights | Why It’s Great for Picnics | |------|-----------------------|----------------------------| | **South Pointe Park** | Downtown Miami, near Ocean Drive | • Scenic ocean views
• Plenty of shaded benches and tables
• Close to restaurants/shops – easy to grab snacks | | **Bayfront Park** | Downtown waterfront along Biscayne Bay | • Wide lawns overlooking the bay
• Picnic shelters available on request
• Kids’ playgrounds nearby | | **Lummus Park** | Surfside Beach, stretches from Collins Ave to Bal Harbour | • Long stretch of beach‑side lawn
• Ideal for sunset picnics
• Nearby cafés for fresh food | | **Flamingo Park** | Near Coral Gables, at the intersection of SW 8th St & Waverly Dr | • Large grassy areas + shade trees
• Dog park adjacent (great for pet owners)
• Easy parking | | **Northshore Open Space** | Across the Rickenbacker Causeway, north of downtown | • Quiet, less crowded than city parks
• Rolling hills perfect for a relaxed lunch outdoors | | **Oleta River State Park** *(just outside Miami)* | Northern edge of Miami-Dade County | • Largest urban state park in FL
• Multiple picnic sites with grills
• Trails, kayaking, bike rentals | ### Tips for Planning Your Picnic 1. **Check Weather Forecast:** Miami can get hot—bring sunscreen, hats, and plenty of water. 2. **Reserve Shelters Early:** For larger groups, call ahead to reserve a pavilion or shelter (most parks allow reservations via their website). 3. **Pack Smart:** Bring reusable plates/bowls, napkins, trash bags, and a cooler with ice packs. 4. **Consider Timing:** Weekday mornings tend to be quieter; weekends can fill up quickly especially during peak season (spring/summer). If you have particular preferences—like wanting a quiet nature setting vs. an active beachfront vibe—or need directions/maps, let me know!
